_comment: Routines policy (mchatai_macOS/docs/ROUTINES_ARCHITECTURE.md §3.3, §4.2, §4.4, §4.5, §8, §9). Read by RoutinePolicy in mChatAI+ (Routines/RoutineContent.swift); the binary carries identical _fallback_only defaults and clamps every value, so a bad edit can't break scheduling. Edit + git push + refreshMchataisourceCache ships with no rebuild. Checked by mchatai_macOS/scripts/check_routine_content.py.

placement._comment: Which process runs each action kind. DERIVED per kind, never chosen by the caller. Swift floor: script can only be shell (the sandboxed app never runs user scripts), every other known kind can only be app (the shell has no pipeline/agent/web/system engine). A value outside that is ignored. Every kind listed here must have routines/actions/<kind>.json.

concurrency._comment: ONE cap shared by routines and the legacy SchedulerService jobs until R3 retires them (§4.4; RunPermitPool in mChatAI+). Legacy first: legacy jobs are capped at this among themselves (exactly as before routines), and a routine starts only while ALL runs (legacy + routines) are under it, so routines never delay a legacy job. Lowering it therefore also serialises the legacy jobs (e.g. 1 = the Daily Brief waits behind a running pipeline) — a RULE #4 change; review it as one. Read at launch (relaunch to apply). Swift clamps to 1-4. Single-flight per routine and one sessionTurn per session apply on top.

lease._comment: §4.2 step 3 / §9 decision 5 (approved): script routines stop when the app hasn't pushed a lease for `days`; the shell warns by notification and menu badge on `warnDay`. Swift clamps days to 2-90 and warnDay to 1..days-1.

retention._comment: routine_runs rows kept per routine and by age (§3.2). Swift clamps maxRunsPerRoutine to 10-1000 and maxAgeDays to 1-365. Running rows are never deleted.

waits._comment: busyWaitMinutes: a sessionTurn routine waits this long for a busy conversation, then records skipped: conversationBusy (§4.5); a routine's own busyWaitMinutes param overrides it. Swift clamps 0-120. approvalWaitMinutes: a blocked unattended turn waits this long for the user, then denies, interrupts and records failed: blockedOnApproval (§9 decision 4). Swift clamps 1-240. pipelineLaneWaitMinutes: how long a scheduled pipeline queues for the single AI Automation pipeline lane (R0 SerialRunGate); consumed from R2. Swift clamps 1-120.

catchUp._comment: Default catch-up when a routine has none of its own (§4.4). once = one run for the latest missed slot if it is within withinHours, otherwise one missed row. skip = a missed row for calendar routines, nothing for intervals. The doc fixes weekly once/72h, daily once/20h and intervals of 6 h or less skip; monthly and longInterval are this file's choice. Swift clamps withinHours to 0-720 and shortInterval.maxSeconds to 0-86400.

retry._comment: R3 (routines replace the legacy scheduler). interruptedMaxRetries: a scheduled slot whose attempt was cut short by a quit (its row is interrupted: appQuit, including an attempt still queued for a run permit or the pipeline lane) is re-run at the next launch under <slot>#retry-<n>, at most this many times per slot; after that one skipped: retryLimitReached row marks the slot handled, so a crash loop stops. The legacy scheduler re-ran such a slot at every launch with no bound; 3 differs from it only when the same slot is cut short 4+ times. 0 = never retry. Swift clamps 0-10.
